modules.title: Single Entry and Incomplete Records
modules.html:
1. Meaning

Single entry describes a system in which the dual aspect of every transaction is not fully recorded. Typically only a cash book and personal accounts of debtors and creditors are kept. Small traders adopt it because it is cheap and simple, but it has serious limitations: no trial balance can be extracted, errors and fraud are hard to detect, and true profit cannot be reliably measured.

2. Profit by Comparison of Capital

A Statement of Affairs (a balance sheet drawn from estimates) is prepared at the start and at the end of the year:

$$ \text{Net Profit} = (\text{Closing Capital} + \text{Drawings}) - (\text{Opening Capital} + \text{Additional Capital}) $$

where capital at each date is simply assets less liabilities.

3. Deriving Missing Figures

Where a trading and profit and loss account is required, the missing totals are computed with total accounts:

$$ \text{Credit Sales} = \text{Closing Debtors} + \text{Receipts from Debtors} + \text{Returns Inwards} + \text{Bad Debts} + \text{Discount Allowed} - \text{Opening Debtors} $$ $$ \text{Credit Purchases} = \text{Closing Creditors} + \text{Payments to Creditors} + \text{Returns Outwards} + \text{Discount Received} - \text{Opening Creditors} $$

Cash and bank summaries reveal drawings and expenses, while mark-up or margin percentages can be used to find missing purchases, sales or closing stock (useful in a stock-loss-by-fire question).

examples.q: On 1 January assets were N2,300,000 and liabilities N700,000. On 31 December assets were N3,400,000 and liabilities N900,000. Drawings during the year were N480,000 and additional capital N200,000. Compute net profit.
Opening debtors N320,000; cash received from debtors N2,150,000; discount allowed N30,000; bad debts N25,000; returns inwards N45,000; closing debtors N410,000. Find credit sales.
examples.a: Credit sales = 410,000 + 2,150,000 + 45,000 + 25,000 + 30,000 - 320,000 = N2,340,000. This is simply the balancing figure of a total debtors account.

modules.title: Accounts of Non-Profit-Making Organisations
modules.html:
1. Terminology

Trading concernNon-profit organisation
CapitalAccumulated Fund
Net profitSurplus of income over expenditure
Net lossDeficit
Trading, Profit and Loss AccountIncome and Expenditure Account
Cash BookReceipts and Payments Account

2. Receipts and Payments Account

A summarised cash book: it records all cash received and paid regardless of period and regardless of whether capital or revenue. It begins and ends with cash/bank balances and shows no surplus or deficit.

3. Income and Expenditure Account

Prepared on the accrual basis, containing only revenue items relating to the current year. Capital receipts (sale of an asset, donations for a building) and capital payments (purchase of equipment) are excluded and go to the balance sheet.

4. Subscriptions

The subscription figure for the year is derived in a subscriptions account:

$$ \text{Subscription Income} = \text{Cash Received} + \text{Arrears at End} + \text{Advance at Start} - \text{Arrears at Start} - \text{Advance at End} $$

Subscriptions in arrears are current assets (subject to prudence); subscriptions in advance are current liabilities.

5. Profit-Making Activities of a Club

A bar or restaurant run by a club has its own Bar Trading Account; only the resulting bar profit is transferred to the Income and Expenditure Account. The opening accumulated fund is found by a statement of affairs:

$$ \text{Accumulated Fund} = \text{Total Assets} - \text{Total Liabilities} $$

examples.q: A club received subscriptions of N960,000 in cash. Arrears were N50,000 at the start and N70,000 at the end; advances were N30,000 at the start and N45,000 at the end. Compute subscription income for the year.
examples.a: Income = 960,000 + 70,000 (closing arrears) + 30,000 (opening advance now earned) - 50,000 (opening arrears received this year) - 45,000 (received in advance for next year) = N965,000. The N70,000 arrears is a current asset and the N45,000 advance a current liability.

examples.q: A club's bar had opening stock N120,000, purchases N860,000, closing stock N140,000 and bar takings N1,300,000. Bar wages were N180,000. Show the bar result and its treatment.
examples.a: Cost of bar sales = 120,000 + 860,000 - 140,000 = N840,000. Gross bar profit = 1,300,000 - 840,000 = N460,000. Less bar wages N180,000 gives a net bar profit of N280,000, which is credited to the Income and Expenditure Account as one line; the individual bar figures do not appear there.

examples.q: Distinguish between the Receipts and Payments Account and the Income and Expenditure Account.
examples.a: The Receipts and Payments Account is a summary of the cash book: it is on a cash basis, includes both capital and revenue items, includes amounts relating to previous and future periods, and starts and ends with cash balances. The Income and Expenditure Account is on an accrual basis, contains only revenue items of the current year, excludes capital items, and ends with a surplus or deficit transferred to the accumulated fund.

modules.title: Statement of affairs and profit by comparison of capital
modules.html:
Statement of affairs and profit by comparison of capital is a key part of Special Accounts (SSS 2, Financial Accounting). Master the meaning, the main points and how it is tested in JAMB and WAEC questions on this topic.

Key points

  • Small traders adopt it because it is cheap and simple, but it has serious limitations: no trial balance can be extracted, errors and fraud are hard to detect, and true profit cannot be reliably measured.
  • Profit by Comparison of Capital A Statement of Affairs (a balance sheet drawn from estimates) is prepared at the start and at the end of the year: $$ \text{Net Profit} = (\text{Closing Capital} + \text{Drawings}) - (\text{Opening Capital} + \text{Additional Capital}) $$ where capital at each date is simply assets less liabilities.
  • Deriving Missing Figures Where a trading and profit and loss account is required, the missing totals are computed with total accounts: $$ \text{Credit Sales} = \text{Closing Debtors} + \text{Receipts from Debtors} + \text{Returns Inwards} + \text{Bad Debts} + \text{Discount Allowed} - \text{Opening Debtors} $$ $$ \text{Credit Purchases} = \text{Closing Creditors} + \text{Payments to Creditors} + \text{Returns Outwards} + \text{Discount Received} - \text{Opening Creditors} $$ Cash and bank summaries reveal drawings and expenses, while mark-up or margin percentages can be used to find missing purchases, sales or closing stock (useful in a stock-loss-by-fire question).
  • Terminology Trading concern Non-profit organisation Capital Accumulated Fund Net profit Surplus of income over expenditure Net loss Deficit Trading, Profit and Loss Account Income and Expenditure Account Cash Book Receipts and Payments Account 2.
  • Receipts and Payments Account A summarised cash book: it records all cash received and paid regardless of period and regardless of whether capital or revenue.

Worked example

Q: The capital of a non-profit-making organisation is called the:
A: Accumulated fund — Clubs and societies describe the excess of assets over liabilities as the accumulated fund.

Q: Which statement is prepared to find opening capital under incomplete records?
A: Statement of affairs — A statement of affairs lists estimated assets and liabilities so that capital can be derived.

examples.q: The capital of a non-profit-making organisation is called the:
examples.a: Accumulated fund — Clubs and societies describe the excess of assets over liabilities as the accumulated fund.

examples.q: Which statement is prepared to find opening capital under incomplete records?
examples.a: Statement of affairs — A statement of affairs lists estimated assets and liabilities so that capital can be derived.

modules.title: Deriving credit sales, credit purchases and missing figures
modules.html:
Deriving credit sales, credit purchases and missing figures is a key part of Special Accounts (SSS 2, Financial Accounting). Master the meaning, the main points and how it is tested in JAMB and WAEC questions on this topic.

Key points

  • Typically only a cash book and personal accounts of debtors and creditors are kept.
  • Deriving Missing Figures Where a trading and profit and loss account is required, the missing totals are computed with total accounts: $$ \text{Credit Sales} = \text{Closing Debtors} + \text{Receipts from Debtors} + \text{Returns Inwards} + \text{Bad Debts} + \text{Discount Allowed} - \text{Opening Debtors} $$ $$ \text{Credit Purchases} = \text{Closing Creditors} + \text{Payments to Creditors} + \text{Returns Outwards} + \text{Discount Received} - \text{Opening Creditors} $$ Cash and bank summaries reveal drawings and expenses, while mark-up or margin percentages can be used to find missing purchases, sales or closing stock (useful in a stock-loss-by-fire question).
  • The balancing figure of the total (control) creditors account gives credit purchases.
  • Only the net bar profit is credited to the income and expenditure account.
  • The balancing figure of the total debtors account yields credit sales when records are incomplete.

Worked example

Q: Credit purchases are found from a:
A: Total creditors account — The balancing figure of the total (control) creditors account gives credit purchases.

Q: Total debtors account is used mainly to determine:
A: Credit sales — The balancing figure of the total debtors account yields credit sales when records are incomplete.

examples.q: Credit purchases are found from a:
examples.a: Total creditors account — The balancing figure of the total (control) creditors account gives credit purchases.

examples.q: Total debtors account is used mainly to determine:
examples.a: Credit sales — The balancing figure of the total debtors account yields credit sales when records are incomplete.

Worked example

Q: The Receipts and Payments Account is essentially a:
A: Summarised cash book — It summarises all cash and bank receipts and payments for the period.

Q: The excess of income over expenditure of a club is called a:

Worked example

Q: The capital of a non-profit-making organisation is called the:
A: Accumulated fund — Clubs and societies describe the excess of assets over liabilities as the accumulated fund.

Q: Subscriptions in arrears at the year end are shown as:
A: A current asset — Amounts owed by members are receivable and therefore a current asset.

examples.q: The capital of a non-profit-making organisation is called the:
examples.a: Accumulated fund — Clubs and societies describe the excess of assets over liabilities as the accumulated fund.

examples.q: Subscriptions in arrears at the year end are shown as:
examples.a: A current asset — Amounts owed by members are receivable and therefore a current asset.

quiz.q: The capital of a non-profit-making organisation is called the:
quiz.solution: Clubs and societies describe the excess of assets over liabilities as the accumulated fund.

quiz.q: Which statement is prepared to find opening capital under incomplete records?
quiz.solution: A statement of affairs lists estimated assets and liabilities so that capital can be derived.

quiz.q: Net profit under single entry equals:
quiz.solution: Drawings are added back and new capital deducted because neither arises from trading.

quiz.q: The Receipts and Payments Account is essentially a:
quiz.solution: It summarises all cash and bank receipts and payments for the period.

quiz.q: Subscriptions in arrears at the year end are shown as:
quiz.solution: Amounts owed by members are receivable and therefore a current asset.

quiz.q: Subscriptions received in advance are:
quiz.solution: They relate to the following year, so they are a liability at the balance sheet date.

quiz.q: The excess of income over expenditure of a club is called a:
quiz.solution: Non-profit bodies use 'surplus' rather than 'profit'.

quiz.q: Purchase of a new club minibus appears in the:
options: Receipts and payments account and balance sheet
quiz.solution: It is a capital payment: shown in the receipts and payments account as cash paid and capitalised in the balance sheet.

quiz.q: Opening capital N900,000, closing capital N1,500,000, drawings N250,000, no new capital. Net profit is:
A major limitation of single entry is that:
options: No trial balance can be extracted
quiz.solution: Because the dual aspect is incomplete, arithmetical accuracy cannot be verified with a trial balance.

quiz.q: Credit purchases are found from a:
quiz.solution: The balancing figure of the total (control) creditors account gives credit purchases.

quiz.q: Profit on a club's bar is transferred to the:
quiz.solution: Only the net bar profit is credited to the income and expenditure account.

quiz.q: Life membership fees are usually treated as:
options: A capital receipt credited to a fund and released over time
quiz.solution: They cover many years, so they are capitalised in a life membership fund and released to income over the membership period.

quiz.q: Which item would NOT appear in an income and expenditure account?
quiz.solution: The purchase of furniture is capital expenditure and belongs in the balance sheet.

quiz.q: Total debtors account is used mainly to determine:
quiz.solution: The balancing figure of the total debtors account yields credit sales when records are incomplete.

quiz.q: A deficit in a club's accounts is:
quiz.solution: An excess of expenditure over income reduces the accumulated fund.

quiz.q: The excess of a non-profit organization's income over its expenditure is called _____.
quiz.solution: Non-profit organizations use the term 'Surplus' instead of profit and 'Deficit' instead of loss.

quiz.q: A credit entry in the Sales Account represents a/an...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Increase in sales.

quiz.q: A Receipts and Payments Account is essentially a summary of the _____.
quiz.solution: A Receipts and Payments account records all cash inflows and outflows of a non-profit organization for a period.

quiz.q: Under incomplete records, profit is calculated by _____.
quiz.solution: This is the 'Capital Comparison' method. Drawings increase the calculated profit, while new capital introduced reduces it.

quiz.q: Income and Expenditure account is used by:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Non-profit organizations.

quiz.q: Receipts and Payments account is a summary of the:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Cash Book.

quiz.q: Receipts and Payments Account is for:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Non-profit organizations.

quiz.q: A Receipts and Payments Account is used by?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Non-profit organizations.

quiz.q: Income and Expenditure Account is similar to?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Profit and Loss Account.

quiz.q: Credit Balance in the Sales Account?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Is normal.

quiz.q: Which book of prime entry is used to record the purchase of a motor van on credit?
quiz.solution: The Purchases Journal is only for credit purchases of goods intended for resale (trading stock). Non-current assets bought on credit are recorded in the General Journal.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a capital expenditure?
options: Purchase of a new delivery truck
quiz.solution: Capital expenditure is spending on non-current assets that will benefit the business for more than one year.

quiz.q: The value of a non-current asset as shown in the books after deducting accumulated depreciation is its _____.
quiz.solution: Net Book Value (NBV) is the historical cost less the total depreciation charged to date.

quiz.q: The list of balances extracted from the ledgers to test the arithmetical accuracy of the double-entry is the _____.
quiz.solution: The Trial Balance is a diagnostic tool to ensure that total debits equal total credits before preparing final accounts.

quiz.q: Which of the following appears on the credit side of the Trading Account?
quiz.solution: Sales and Closing Stock are credited to the Trading Account to calculate the gross profit.

quiz.q: The account maintained for each head of expenditure in the Public Sector is the _____.
quiz.solution: In government accounting, a 'Vote' is the authority to spend money on a specific head of expenditure.

quiz.q: The value of a non-current asset after deducting accumulated depreciation is its _____.
quiz.solution: Net Book Value (NBV) is the historical cost of an asset minus the total depreciation charged against it since its acquisition.

quiz.q: A Statement of Affairs is prepared to determine the _____.
quiz.solution: In single-entry systems, a Statement of Affairs (Assets minus Liabilities) is prepared at the start of the period to find the opening capital.

quiz.q: The double entry principle for a cash sale is:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Debit Cash, Credit Sales.

quiz.q: Capital Expenditure is expenditure on:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Acquisition of fixed assets.

quiz.q: The double entry for selling goods for cash is:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Dr Cash, Cr Sales.

quiz.q: A statement of affairs is similar to a:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Balance sheet.

quiz.q: Capital Expenditure:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Buying Fixed Assets.

quiz.q: Source document for credit sales:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Sales Invoice.

quiz.q: Incomplete records occur when a business does not maintain a full...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Double entry system.

quiz.q: Double entry principle states that:
options: Debit the receiver, Credit the giver
Credit the receiver, Debit the giver
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Debit the receiver, Credit the giver.

quiz.q: Double Entry:
quiz.solution: Past question (NECO 2025). Correct answer: Debit Receiver, Credit Giver.

quiz.q: Receipts & Payments:
quiz.solution: Past question (NECO 2025). Correct answer: Cash summary (Non-profit).

quiz.q: Income & Expenditure:
quiz.solution: Past question (NECO 2025). Correct answer: Like P&L (Non-profit).

quiz.q: Accumulated Fund:
quiz.solution: Past question (NECO 2025). Correct answer: Capital (Non-profit).

quiz.q: Receipts & Payments A/c:
quiz.solution: Past question (WAEC 2025). Correct answer: Non-profit.

quiz.q: Sales Journal records:
quiz.solution: Past question (WAEC 2025). Correct answer: Credit Sales.

quiz.q: The double-entry system states that?
options: Every credit must have a debit
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Every credit must have a debit.

quiz.q: A Credit Balance in the Bank Statement indicates?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Money in the bank.
